evidence.title: Ishango (Semliki Valley, DR Congo): Late Pleistocene Barbed Harpoons & Notched Bone
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon and amino-acid racemization on Semliki terrace shells and mammal bone
evidence.summary: Where the Semliki River leaves Lake Edward, stratified shoreline levels preserve lakeside fishing camps with quartzite microliths, double-row barbed bone harpoons, and the famous Ishango bone handle incised with grouped notches.
evidence.limits: Calcareous shell beds created hard-water radiocarbon offsets before Brooks & Smith (1987) re-dated the sequence to ~25–20 ka.

evidence.title: Matupi Cave (Ituri Rainforest, NE DR Congo): Late Pleistocene Equatorial Foraging
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon charcoal sequence across Late Pleistocene and Holocene cave strata
evidence.summary: Carved into Mount Hoyo limestone inside the northeastern Congo rainforest, Matupi Cave preserves a >40,000-year sequence of quartz microliths, bored stones, and Holocene forest-edge hunting deposits.
evidence.limits: Tropical soil acidity destroyed unmineralized organics in lower levels; pollen indicates forest–savanna shifts over time.

evidence.title: Gombe / Kalina Point (Kinshasa, DR Congo): Lupemban-to-Tshitolian Sequence
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified Congo River sands with radiocarbon and typological Lupemban–Tshitolian–ceramic benchmarks
evidence.summary: At the Pool Malebo outlet of the Congo River, deep windblown and alluvial sands preserve Lupemban lanceolate points, Tshitolian geometric microliths, and early pottery horizons across 45 millennia.
evidence.limits: Bioturbation and sandy colluviation require refit analyses to separate Pleistocene Lupemban knapping floors from Holocene pits.

evidence.title: Ngovo Cave (Kongo Central, Lower Congo): Stone-to-Metal Axes & Early Pottery
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon dates on associated charcoal and oil-palm endocarps
evidence.summary: Excavated in Lower Congo karst hills, Ngovo Cave defines a pivotal Stone-to-Metal Age tradition combining edge-ground stone axes, abundant oil-palm kernels (*Elaeis guineensis*), and thick flat-based ceramics.
evidence.limits: Ngovo contexts immediately precede or overlap early ironworking without iron objects recovered inside the type cave itself.

evidence.title: Dimba & Sakuzi Caves (Lower Congo, DR Congo): Terminal Pleistocene Microliths to Ceramics
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon charcoal sequence spanning Tshitolian to early ceramic horizons
evidence.summary: Limestone caves near Mbanza-Ngungu preserve a multi-millennial transition from Late Pleistocene–Holocene Tshitolian hunting assemblages into early woodland pottery and arboricultural pit features.
evidence.limits: Cave palimpsests compress slow sedimentary accumulation across arid–humid Holocene phases.

evidence.title: Tshikapa & Kasai Valley Terraces (Southern DR Congo): Lupemban Bifaces
evidence.dateBasis: Alluvial terrace stratigraphy and re-appraised Middle-to-Later Stone Age techno-typology
evidence.summary: High terraces along the Kasai River around Tshikapa yielded classic Lupemban finely thinned lanceolate foliate points and heavy core-axes adapted to forest–savanna gallery woodlands.
evidence.limits: Diamond-mining gravel exposures provide rich typological series but few undisturbed primary living floors.

evidence.title: Kamoa River Basin (Upper Katanga, SE DR Congo): Stratified Acheulean to LSA
evidence.dateBasis: River-terrace stratigraphy, charcoal radiocarbon for LSA levels, and lithic technocomplex correlation
evidence.summary: Along the Upper Congo–Zambezi divide west of Kolwezi, Kamoa preserves sequential Acheulean handaxes, Sangoan–Lupemban core-axes, and Nachikufan Later Stone Age quartz hunting tools.
evidence.limits: Pleistocene ferricrete horizons rely on stratigraphic correlation whereas only upper Holocene levels have radiocarbon dates.

evidence.title: Mukinanira & Lake Kivu Western Highlands (Eastern DR Congo): Early Iron Smelting
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon charcoal dates from shaft iron-smelting furnaces and Urewe ceramics
evidence.summary: Highland furnace pits and bevel-rimmed Urewe ceramics west of Lake Kivu document early Great Lakes iron metallurgy, brick-built furnace shafts, and cleared montane woodland agriculture.
evidence.limits: Old-wood effects on hardwood charcoal samples are assessed by paired short-lived botanical remains.

evidence.title: Bondongo-Losombo (Ngiri Floodplain, NW DR Congo): Equatorial Swamp-Forest Pottery
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon charcoal from seasonally inundated riverine settlement pits
evidence.summary: Raised levee sites along the Ngiri tributary between the Ubangi and Congo rivers yield early incised riverine pottery and evidence of specialized swamp-forest fishing communities before 100 CE.
evidence.limits: Seasonal inundation limits deep horizontal excavation outside dry-season windows.

evidence.title: Mbandaka & Ruki Confluence (Equateur, DR Congo): Imbonga Ceramic Hearth Pits
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon charcoal and palm-nut dates from Imbonga-horizon refuse pits
evidence.summary: At the Ruki–Congo confluence in the central rainforest core, large bell-shaped pits preserve Imbonga rocker-stamped vessels, charred oil-palm nuts, and Canarium schweinfurthii incense resin fruits.
evidence.limits: Acidic oxisols preserve ceramics and charred endocarps while unburned faunal bone rarely survives.

evidence.title: Lusambo & Sankuru Basin (Central DR Congo): Forest–Savanna Ecotone Occupations
evidence.dateBasis: Holocene lithic and early ceramic horizon dates across the southern Congo rim
evidence.summary: River bluffs along the Sankuru bridge the inner Congo rainforest and southern savannas, yielding Holocene microlithic workshops followed by first-millennium BCE ceramic and early metal-using settlements.
evidence.limits: Large expanses of the Kasai–Sankuru basin remain less intensively sampled than the Kwilu and lower Congo corridors.

evidence.title: Boyoma Falls / Upper Congo Bend (Tshopo, NE DR Congo): Cataract Forager-Settlers
evidence.dateBasis: Lithic-to-early-ceramic riverbank stratigraphy and regional Congo radiocarbon correlation
evidence.summary: At the seven cataracts connecting the Lualaba and middle Congo rivers, riverbank deposits document specialized cataract fishing and early ceramic connections extending toward the Ituri and central basin.
evidence.limits: Detailed excavation coverage around Kisangani remains patchy relative to later colonial disturbance.

evidence.title: Oboui & Gbabiri (Nana-Mambéré, Western CAR): Earliest Central African Ironworking
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon series on charcoal from bloomery forges and reduction furnaces
evidence.summary: On the granite plateaus of western Central African Republic, Oboui and Gbabiri preserve tuyeres, slag pits, hammerstones, and bloomery forges yielding second-millennium BCE radiocarbon determinations for early iron reduction.
evidence.limits: Whether iron smelting began around ~2000 BCE or closer to ~1000–800 BCE due to old-wood effects remains an active scholarly debate.

evidence.title: Batalimo & Lobaye Valley (Southern CAR): Ubangi Rainforest Pottery & Stone Axes
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon dates on carbonized botanical remains and ceramic pit fills
evidence.summary: Along the lower Lobaye tributary of the Ubangi, Batalimo-Maluba sites reveal settled villages with distinctive grooved ceramics, polished hematite axes, and oil-palm management on the northern forest rim.
evidence.limits: Recent re-dating by Seidensticker places classic Batalimo ceramic phases squarely in the last centuries BCE to early CE.

evidence.title: Bangui & Ubangi Rapids (Southern CAR): Pre-100 CE Slag Mounds & Stone Industries
evidence.dateBasis: Furnace radiocarbon dates and river-terrace ceramic/lithic sequences
evidence.summary: Rocky rapids where the Ubangi turns south into the Congo Basin preserve both earlier quartz stone assemblages and first-millennium BCE–early CE bloomery iron-smelting workshops.
evidence.limits: Urban growth across modern Bangui has truncated parts of the riverside terrace stratigraphy.

evidence.title: Ndélé & Bamingui-Bangoran Escarpment (Northern CAR): Savanna Rockshelters
evidence.dateBasis: Holocene Later Stone Age and early iron-horizon shelter sequences
evidence.summary: Sandstone escarpments on the Chad–Congo watershed harbor rockshelters with Holocene quartz microliths, geometric paintings, and early iron-using pastoral–forager camps bridging the Sudanic belt.
evidence.limits: Remote savanna escarpments have received limited modern excavation compared to western CAR.

evidence.title: Toulou & Lengo Sandstone Shelters (Eastern CAR): Engravings & LSA Camps
evidence.dateBasis: Association with Later Stone Age microlithic and early ceramic shelter fills
evidence.summary: East of Bangassou near the Mbomou–Chinko drainage, sandstone slabs at Toulou and Lengo preserve pecked throwing-knife, spear, and animal engravings alongside Later Stone Age occupation floors.
evidence.limits: Open-air rock engravings lack direct pigment binding agents and are bracketed via shelter deposits.

evidence.title: Tchissanga (Kouilou Coast, Rep. of the Congo): Early Coastal Pottery & Transition
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon charcoal dates from refuse pits across coastal savanna ridges
evidence.summary: Excavated by James Denbow north of Pointe-Noire, Tchissanga preserves hundreds of comb-stamped vessels, charred palm kernels, and grindstones marking early settled coastal communities along the Atlantic.
evidence.limits: Tchissanga represents a pre-metallurgical village phase immediately predating coastal iron-smelting sites nearby.

evidence.title: Madingo-Kayes & Loango Littoral (Rep. of the Congo): Shell Middens & Iron Onset
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon series on estuarine shell middens and early ironworking pits
evidence.summary: Sandspits and lagoons of the Loango littoral preserve Stone Age campsites overlain by early ceramic villages and Early Iron Age shell-and-slag middens exploiting estuarine fisheries and oil palm.
evidence.limits: Holocene shoreline erosion has reworked some low-lying Atlantic lagoon deposits.

evidence.title: Ntamo / Brazzaville Rapids & Bateke Plateau: Tshitolian to Early Metallurgy
evidence.dateBasis: Paleosol radiocarbon dates from sandy plateau ridges above Pool Malebo
evidence.summary: Opposite Kinshasa on the Bateke Plateau margins, stratified Kalahari Sands preserve terminal Pleistocene–Holocene Tshitolian projectile armatures followed by early pottery and iron-smelting workshops by the last centuries BCE.
evidence.limits: Aeolian sand reworking requires careful paleosol micromorphology to verify primary context.

evidence.title: Ouesso & Sangha–Likouala Confluence (Northern Rep. of the Congo): Rainforest Villages
evidence.dateBasis: AMS charcoal and palm-kernel dates from forested river-bank pits
evidence.summary: Where the Sangha River traverses the Middle Holocene rainforest corridor, early ceramic pits show rapid canoe-borne settlement linking Cameroon–CAR tributaries with the central Congo Basin.
evidence.limits: Survey density follows navigable riverbanks while deep interfluves remain largely unexplored.

evidence.title: Otoumbi & Middle Ogooué Furnaces (Gabon): Early Forest Iron Smelting
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon charcoal dates inside intact bloomery pit furnaces
evidence.summary: Along savanna patches flanking the Middle Ogooué, Otoumbi preserves some of west-central Africa's earliest dated bloomery iron-smelting furnaces alongside stone-lined hearths and Okanda ceramics.
evidence.limits: Debate continues over whether a few ~6th–5th century BCE dates reflect genuine early smelting or older residual charcoal.

evidence.title: Okala (Estuary Peninsula, NW Gabon): Neolithic-Stage Refuse Pits & Ground Axes
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon dates on palm endocarps and hearth charcoal from hilltop pit clusters
evidence.summary: Excavated just north of Libreville, Okala defines Gabon's pre-iron ceramic village horizon with flat-bottomed decorated pots, dolerite polished axes, hoes, and abundant oil-palm cultivation before 100 BCE.
evidence.limits: Iron artifacts are absent from Okala refuse pits, distinguishing it from neighboring slightly later iron-bearing estuary sites.

evidence.title: Moanda & Haut-Ogooué Plateau (SE Gabon): Early Metallurgy & Manganese Highlands
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon furnace dates and plateau LSA–EIA sequence
evidence.summary: Southeastern Gabon's savanna-mosaic plateaus around Moanda yielded Later Stone Age quartz tool scatters followed by early first-millennium BCE–CE iron-smelting sites exploiting high-grade ores.
evidence.limits: Surface Later Stone Age scatters often lack stratified organics beneath ironworking layers.

evidence.title: Corisco Island & Mbini Estuary (Equatorial Guinea): Early Iron Burials & Insular Maritime Camps
evidence.dateBasis: AMS radiocarbon dates on funerary charcoal and offshore shell–ceramic contexts
evidence.summary: On tiny Corisco Island off Equatorial Guinea, excavations uncovered ritual pit burials furnished with iron blades, bracelets, spoon-shaped ceremonial irons, and Oveng-related pottery spanning the first millennium BCE to early CE.
evidence.limits: Humid tropical island sands dissolve human bone rapidly, leaving metal grave offerings and vessel impressions as primary evidence.

evidence.title: Nkang (Central Cameroon): Earliest African Banana Phytoliths & Refuse Pits
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon charcoal and oil-palm dates from pit fills containing Musa phytoliths
evidence.summary: North of Yaoundé, Nkang refuse pits preserve domesticated Asian plantain/banana (*Musa*) phytoliths alongside sheep/goat bones, polished stone axes, and ceramics — evidence for early trans-continental crop dispersal across the forest.
evidence.limits: Exact arrival vectors of *Musa* across East-Central Africa before 500 BCE remain under active archaeobotanical investigation.

evidence.title: Bwambé-Sommet & Kribi Coast (SW Cameroon): Pearl Millet in Rainforest Pits
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS radiocarbon on charred Pennisetum glaucum grains from coastal village pits
evidence.summary: Coastal ridge settlements south of Kribi preserve directly dated charred pearl millet (*Pennisetum glaucum*) alongside oil palm and Canarium trees, revealing that Late Holocene forest gaps permitted Sahelian cereal cultivation inside southern Cameroon.
evidence.limits: Archaeobotanical sampling confirms seasonal forest clearance without proving continuous multi-century occupation at individual pits.

evidence.title: Abang Minko'o & Oliga (Southern Cameroon Border): Early Iron & Forest Farming
evidence.dateBasis: Direct AMS dates on charred pearl millet grains, oil palm, and ironworking hearths
evidence.summary: Excavations near Ambam near the Cameroon–Gabon–Equatorial Guinea tri-border documented first-millennium BCE refuse pits combining pearl millet grains, Canarium, oil palm, and early iron production.
evidence.limits: Pit clusters represent shifting village homesteads along forest–corridor clearings rather than fortified town centers.

evidence.title: Mbi Crater & Fiye Nkwi (Cameroon Grassfields): Mid-Holocene Highland Shelters
evidence.dateBasis: Highland crater-lake pollen cores paired with Bamenda Escarpment rockshelter radiocarbon dates
evidence.summary: Surrounding Shum Laka at 1,600–2,100 m elevation, volcanic crater cores and Bamenda shelters record early basalt hoe-making, wild-to-managed oil-palm expansion, and ancestral Bantu-homeland hunter–horticulturist shifts.
evidence.limits: Volcanic highland soils dissolve uncarbonized bone outside alkaline shelter deposits.

evidence.title: Salak & Diamaré Plain (Far North Cameroon): Pre-Sao Floodplain Villages
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified tell basal radiocarbon dates across the Diamaré piedmont
evidence.summary: Between the Mandara Mountains and Logone floodplain, basal mound layers at Salak record early Iron Age villages, sorghum/millet subsistence, and regional trade linking Lake Chad with central savannas.
evidence.limits: Upper mound occupation continues later into the first millennium CE; basal dates anchor initial village formation.

evidence.title: Mdaga & Chari-Logone Mounds (SW Chad): Earliest Floodplain Tells & Clay Figurines
evidence.dateBasis: Basal mound radiocarbon dates along the lower Chari delta
evidence.summary: On elevated clay islands near the Chari–Logone confluence, Mdaga's deepest levels preserve fishing–agropastoralist settlements, early ironwork, and fired terracotta figurines centuries before classical Sao walled towns.
evidence.limits: Deep tell stratigraphy beneath 5 m of later occupation restricts large horizontal exposure of the oldest layers.

evidence.title: Chari-Baguirmi & Southern Mega-Chad Shorelines (Central Chad): Holocene Fisher-Herders
evidence.dateBasis: Paleolake beach-ridge radiocarbon dates and impressed ceramic–bone harpoon assemblages
evidence.summary: Along receding Holocene shoreline ridges south and east of Lake Chad, fisher-forager camps gave way after ~2000 BCE to mobile cattle herders and early iron-using settlements along the Bahr el-Ghazal paleochannel.
evidence.limits: Wind deflation across ancient sand-dune ridges compresses multiple Holocene occupational visits.

evidence.title: Moundou & Upper Logone Floodplain (Southern Chad): Savanna LSA & Early Iron Villages
evidence.dateBasis: Regional Sudanic-savanna radiocarbon ironworking and ceramic correlations
evidence.summary: Along the Upper Logone riverbanks connecting CAR's ironworking plateaus with Lake Chad's clay plains, early savanna settlements combined riverine fishing, wild yam/millet tending, and early bloomery iron smelting.
evidence.limits: Southern Chad's Logone corridor remains underrepresented in modern systematic fieldwork compared to northern Cameroon.

evidence.title: Lokabulo Rockshelter (Eastern Equatoria, South Sudan): Stratified LSA & Early Pottery
evidence.dateBasis: Radiocarbon dates on shelter charcoal across quartz LSA and early pastoral layers
evidence.summary: Excavated in granite inselbergs east of Juba, Lokabulo preserves a stratified sequence from Later Stone Age quartz microlith hunters into early pottery-making and domestic stock-tending communities before 100 CE.
evidence.limits: Large portions of Equatoria and Upper Nile have seen few excavations since Nicholas David's 1979 survey.

evidence.title: Dungo IV & V (Baía Farta, Coastal Angola): Pleistocene Whale-Carcass Tool Use
evidence.dateBasis: Cosmogenic nuclide burial ages and raised marine-terrace stratigraphy
evidence.summary: On raised marine terraces south of Benguela, Dungo IV preserves dozens of quartz flakes, choppers, and picks tightly clustered around a fossilized baleen whale skeleton—rare Earlier-to-Middle Stone Age evidence of Atlantic coastal scavenging.
evidence.limits: Radiometric age estimates span >350 ka to earlier Pleistocene brackets depending on cosmogenic model assumptions.

evidence.title: Chitato & Lunda Norte (NE Angola): Lupemban-to-Tshitolian Kasai Headwaters
evidence.dateBasis: Kasai tributary terrace stratigraphy and Lupemban–Tshitolian lithic re-appraisal
evidence.summary: Alluvial terraces of the Chicapa and Luachimo rivers in northeastern Angola preserve classic Lupemban bifaces, Sangoan heavy picks, and Tshitolian barbed arrowheads linking southern savanna woodlands with the Congo Basin.
evidence.limits: Mid-20th-century diamond-pit collections rely on stratigraphic correlation rather than high-precision OSL or AMS series.
